exactPassages: Sidewalk cafes provided beyond the building line shall comply with the requirements of this section, the New York City Zoning Resolution, the Commissioners of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation, and with the projection limitations of Chapter 32 of this code.
No part of any awning, enclosure, fixture, equipment or removable platform of a sidewalk cafe shall be located:
2. So as to obstruct any exit from a building;
3. So as to obstruct any cellar access hatch or areaway;

Exception: Upon special application, the commissioner may permit an easily removable, prominently designated platform, designed in accordance with Section 3111.5, to cover a cellar entrance or areaway that is not used as a required means of egress.
Sidewalk cafes and access thereto shall comply with Chapter 11.

Where dining surfaces for the consumption of food or drink are provided, at least 10 percent of the total number of seating and standing spaces, but not less than one, of each type of dining surfaces shall be accessible and be distributed throughout the facility and located on a level accessed by an accessible route.

Unless separated from seating inside the building by fire partitions complying with Section 713 , the seating for enclosed sidewalk cafes shall be added to that inside the building in order to determine whether a place of assembly certificate of operation is required.

testCase.question: A restaurant proposes a sidewalk café with furniture near a building exit and cellar hatch. The owner says outdoor-dining authorization allows the exterior seats to be counted separately from the interior PACO and eliminates further accessibility review. The documents do not say whether the café is beyond the building line, enclosed, or separated from the interior seating by a Section 713 fire partition. What can be concluded from the selected Building Code passages, and what remains unresolved?
testCase.expectedConclusion: The proposal cannot be approved from the selected evidence. If it is a sidewalk café beyond the building line, BC 3111.1 requires compliance not only with Section 3111 but also with Chapter 32 and separate zoning and agency requirements; the selected evidence does not provide those outside rules. BC 3111.4 prohibits café components from obstructing a building exit or cellar hatch. Its cellar-entrance exception is not automatic: it requires a special application, an easily removable and prominently designated platform designed under Section 3111.5, and a cellar entrance or areaway that is not required egress. BC 3111.6 makes Chapter 11 applicable to the café and its access. BC 1108.2.9.1 requires accessible seating and standing spaces equal to at least 10 percent of the total, with not less than one accessible space at each type of dining surface; those spaces must be distributed and located on a level served by an accessible route. BC 3111.7 supplies only a conditional rule for an enclosed sidewalk café: unless a Section 713 fire partition separates it from inside seating, its seating is added to the inside seating solely to determine whether a PACO is required. These passages do not establish the approved interior capacity, the treatment of every open exterior seating arrangement, property-line or operational jurisdiction, DOT authorization, electrical permitting, or overall approval.

expectedUncertainty.description: The selected passages establish several conditional Building Code constraints, but they do not establish overall approval, current agency jurisdiction, lawful seating capacity, or electrical and operational requirements.

answer.answerText:
The owner’s position is not supported by these selected Building Code passages. If the proposed café is beyond the building line, it must comply not only with BC 3111 but also with the Zoning Resolution, applicable Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation commissioner requirements, and Chapter 32 projection limitations. The stated outdoor-dining authorization does not, on this evidence, eliminate those requirements or the separate accessibility requirement.

Furniture, equipment, enclosures, removable platforms, and awnings for a sidewalk café may not obstruct a building exit or a cellar access hatch/areaway. The supplied evidence does not establish compliance because the exit and hatch geometry and the placement dimensions are unknown. A platform may cover a cellar entrance or areaway only if the commissioner permits it upon special application, it is easily removable and prominently designated, it complies with BC 3111.5, and the entrance/areaway is not used as a required means of egress. The selected evidence does not establish any of those exception conditions.

Accessibility review remains required: the sidewalk café and its access must comply with Chapter 11. Where dining surfaces are provided, at least 10 percent of the total seating and standing spaces—and at least one of each dining-surface type—must be accessible, distributed throughout the facility, and located on a level reached by an accessible route. The accessible dining-surface distribution, the dining-surface types, total seating/standing spaces, and accessible-route conditions are not provided, so compliance cannot be determined.

Exterior seats are not automatically counted separately for the place-of-assembly certificate-of-operation question. For an enclosed sidewalk café, its seating must be added to inside seating unless the café is separated from that seating by fire partitions complying with Section 713. Because enclosure status, the interior and exterior seat counts, and the existence and Section 713 compliance of any separating fire partition are unknown, the selected evidence does not resolve whether combined seating triggers a place-of-assembly certificate of operation. The selected passages also do not provide the threshold for when that certificate is required.

The building and property-line locations must be established before determining whether the specific beyond-building-line rule applies. Current agency authorizations should also be verified; the supplied Building Code text identifies other agency and zoning requirements but does not establish what authorization has been issued or whether it satisfies them.
answer.conclusion: The owner’s position is not supported by these selected Building Code passages. If the proposed café is beyond the building line, it must comply not only with BC 3111 but also with the Zoning Resolution, applicable Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation commissioner requirements, and Chapter 32 projection limitations. The stated outdoor-dining authorization does not, on this evidence, eliminate those requirements or the separate accessibility requirement.

supportedPoints.explanation: For an enclosed sidewalk café, seating must be added to inside seating to determine whether a place-of-assembly certificate of operation is required, unless it is separated from inside seating by fire partitions complying with Section 713.

supportedPoints.heading: Accessible dining-surface quantity and distribution
supportedPoints.explanation: The dining-surface rule requires accessible seating and standing spaces equal to at least 10 percent of the total, with a minimum of one of each dining-surface type; accessible dining surfaces must also be distributed throughout the facility and be on a level accessed by an accessible route.
